transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, doctor. Thank you. Well, what finally pushed me to come in today is that I'm having a really hard time keeping my focus at work. 

I manage a clinic, and... well, I can start an EPIC quality report, or sit down in a metrics meeting with every intention of paying attention and tracking it. But within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far off. I'll catch myself rereading the exact same numbers over and over, or I'll suddenly realize I completely missed the whole point of the discussion. It's just getting really frustrating to deal with.
When did you first start noticing these concentration problems? Have you always had difficulty focusing, or is this something new that's developed more recently?

Well, I'd say I really started noticing it about two years and four months ago. I got a promotion right around then, which meant taking on a much larger portfolio at the clinic. 

I think... before that, I had systems I relied on to keep myself on track, and they worked okay for me. But once my responsibilities grew, those old systems just got completely overwhelmed. So, that's when it really became a problem.

Besides the difficulty concentrating, have you noticed that you feel restless, fidgety, or like you have excess energy that's hard to contain? Or do you find yourself acting on impulse without thinking things through?
No, I wouldn't say I feel restless or fidgety. I don't really have excess energy, either. And I don't think I act on impulse... it's really just the focus and concentration that I struggle with.
Over these past two years, have you noticed changes in your mood? For example, do you feel sad, empty, or less interested in things you normally enjoy?

No, not really. I don't feel sad or empty, and I still enjoy my usual activities outside of the clinic. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself at work because of the focus issues, but my overall mood is fine.

Around the time you got promoted and started having these concentration problems two years ago, did you experience any medical illnesses, start any new medications, or notice any other changes in your physical health or how you felt physically?

No, nothing like that. I didn't have any new illnesses or start any new medications back then. Honestly, physically, I felt exactly the same as I always had. There weren't any health changes at all around the time of the promotion, just the extra workload.

When you're not at work—say, when you're doing something you enjoy or relaxing at home—do you find it easy to focus and concentrate on that activity, or do you struggle with attention in those situations too?

No, I haven't really noticed it being a problem at home. If I'm doing something I enjoy, or just relaxing, I can usually focus just fine. It's... it really just seems to happen at the clinic, when I'm trying to get through all the management tasks and paperwork. So, yeah, outside of work, my attention seems okay.

When you're at work but doing something simpler or more routine—like administrative tasks that don't require as much mental effort—do you find yourself able to concentrate better on those, or do you still struggle with focus no matter what you're doing at the clinic?

I'm not really sure if there's a difference, to be honest. Um, actually, those routine administrative tasks are a big part of what I struggle with. The paperwork and the basic management stuff... I just can't seem to stay on track with any of it. So, no, I wouldn't say I concentrate any better on the simpler things. I just struggle to keep my focus on work tasks in general.

When you're at work, are there any specific types of tasks—like ones that require you to hold multiple pieces of information in your mind at once, or make decisions based on complex information—where your concentration problems feel worse compared to simpler, more straightforward tasks?

Honestly, no, I haven't really noticed it being worse with one type of task over another. Like I was just saying with the routine stuff, it's all kind of difficult right now. I don't think having to juggle a lot of information or make complex decisions makes my focus any worse than when I'm just trying to get through standard paperwork. It really just feels like a struggle across the board with everything at the clinic, no matter how complicated the task is.

Before you got promoted two years ago, when you had those systems in place that helped you stay on track—do you remember if you had ever struggled with concentration or focus even back then, but just managed it better with those organizational systems? Or was your attention genuinely sharp and easy for you before the promotion?

Well, if I really think back... I guess I've always had some trouble with it, actually. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. And my mother used to have to sit right there with me while I did my homework, because otherwise I'd just lose track of what I was supposed to be doing, or I'd forget to bring my books home from school altogether. So, yeah, I suppose the focus issues have always been there, I just had ways of dealing with it before the promotion.
